fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Moses gave the law to “…the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.” That's two groups holding it, not just one person. Me, I'd be nervous with only one keeper, because my hands are a mustache and I once dropped a whole tray of dough with them.

Nice thought, friend, but this song isn't a victory song. The LORD has Moses write it down and teach it to the Israelites so it stands as a witness for Him against them. He also says it “…will not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants.” Crossing the Jordan isn't what it's for.

problems.problem: Saying Papa wouldn't trust his recipe to one person either implies Moses shared that distrust. The text doesn't give that as Moses' reason for handing the law to both groups.
The smoke detector comparison suggests a warning device, rather than a song that testifies against the people. The comparison doesn't match the song's stated role.
